title: Executive Summary
headline: The system is built and every line for the next three days is live, with a source link on every row. The out-of-sample window is now 51 games rather than 28. The honest read on it: the model has a small edge on the margin, no edge on totals or winners, and one strategy whose good record is still well inside what luck produces.
lead: Ten strategies were written, seven validation gates were defined, and all ten were run against a strictly out-of-sample window: all 51 completed games from 2026-11-06 to 2026-11-12, every one of them predicted using team ratings computed only from 2026-10-20 to 2026-11-05. No game in the test window contributes to the ratings that predict it.

verdict.one_line: The model beats the naive reference on margin accuracy and loses to it on totals and on picking winners. The best strategy is 16-7, worth +7.55 model units - but with an exact p-value of 0.093 and a Wilson lower bound of 0.491 against a 0.524 break-even, it fails the skill gate. Every strategy stays at quarter-unit or research-only.
verdict.why: Fifty-one games with a 17.4-point residual standard deviation narrows the uncertainty a lot but does not remove it. On 23 graded plays, a 16-7 run happens often enough by chance that it cannot be called skill.

findings.title: The model wins on the margin and loses on totals and winners
findings.detail: Margin: MAE 12.89 against 13.19 for the naive reference, RMSE 17.10 against 17.70 - the model is better on both. Totals: MAE 14.86 against 14.75, RMSE 19.88 against 19.59 - the reference is better on both. Straight up both went 37-14, but the reference has the better Brier score (0.1889 against 0.1970) and the better log loss (0.5567 against 0.5768).
findings.reading: The refinements buy a real but tiny margin improvement and nothing else. The probability calibration is the weakest part of the model, and it is where the remaining work should go.

findings.title: Growing the window from 28 games to 51 changed a conclusion - which is the most useful thing that happened
findings.detail: On the 28-game window the model beat the reference on totals (MAE 14.50 against 14.75). On 51 games it does not (14.86 against 14.75). The sign flipped. That is exactly the failure mode the sample gate exists to catch, and it is why nothing here is being promoted on the earlier reading.
findings.reading: Any single-window result at this sample size should be treated as a hypothesis, not a finding.

findings.title: The best strategy is 16-7, and that is not enough
findings.detail: S1 (side edge vs the reference spread) produced 23 graded plays at 16-7, worth +7.55 model units and a 32.8% return at -110. Its exact binomial p-value against a coin flip is 0.093. The Wilson 95% interval on its hit rate is 0.491 to 0.844, and the lower bound is below the 0.5238 break-even, so the skill gate fails. S5 (back-to-back fade) is 8-4 on 12 plays, also short.
findings.reading: A 69.6% hit rate on 23 plays is a promising signal and nothing more. The leaderboard caps it at quarter-unit regardless of its score, which is the designed behaviour.

findings.title: Home court looks normal; the back-to-back penalty is large but uncertain
findings.detail: Home-court advantage estimates at +2.79 points with a standard error of 2.48 (t = 1.12), squarely in the historical NBA range. The back-to-back penalty estimates at -6.10 points with a standard error of 4.87 (t = -1.25); because |t| >= 1 the model applies the full 6.10, but the standard error is most of the estimate and detection is still incomplete for 2026-11-06, which biases it toward zero.
findings.reading: Both are published with their standard errors and both are fitted on the test window, which is disclosed on every row they touch.

findings.title: Shrinkage was derived rather than guessed, and the curve is flat where it matters
findings.detail: The empirical-Bayes calculation gives k = 2.9, weighting each team's observed net rating at 0.739. The fixed-k sweep shows margin MAE moving only from 13.28 at k = 0 to 12.91 at k = 4, then degrading to 13.65 by k = 20. Heavy shrinkage is clearly wrong; the choice between light and none barely matters.
findings.reading: The constant is defensible, its sensitivity is published, and it is not a source of hidden risk.

findings.title: Availability impact is a measured floor, not an estimate
findings.detail: Minutes are only known for the 50 players in the captured official table. Players outside it contribute 0.00 to the impact, so teams missing rotation players who are not top-50 scorers show a smaller number than the truth - sometimes zero. The minutes-coverage column sits next to every figure so a 0.00 is never read as 'healthy'.
findings.reading: Correct but incomplete - the Injuries page says so on every row rather than hiding it.

findings.title: Correlation is measured where it can be and flagged where it cannot
findings.detail: Thirteen team-statistic pairs were measured directly on all 30 teams from the official advanced table. Net rating explains 87% of the variation in win percentage; pace is nearly unrelated to net rating (r = -0.34, p = 0.063) and assist percentage is unrelated to offensive efficiency (r = 0.02, p = 0.92). The parlay and same-game-parlay correlations that drive pricing are model-derived and labelled as such.
findings.reading: The distinction matters most for parlays, because pricing correlated legs as independent is the classic way to overpay.

findings.title: The word 'edge' on this site does not mean edge against a sportsbook
findings.detail: No sportsbook price is published by an NBA-operated source, so no official link can be attached to one. The site bets the originated line against a deliberately naive reference model built from the same official ratings. Until real prices are logged, 'units won' means model-vs-naive-model units.
findings.reading: This is the single most important caveat for anyone reading the leaderboard.

what_is_live_now: Originated spreads, totals, moneylines and fair prices for all 23 games across 2026-11-13, 2026-11-14 and 2026-11-15.
43 picks from the strategy library, each tagged with its strategy, its market, the reference number it is betting against, the model's number and the gap.
Player projections for the top-50 scorers, with the possession, opponent-defence and teammate-availability factors broken out separately.
The official injury report for 2026-11-13 and 2026-11-14, transcribed row by row with each player's status and the team's published reason.
Game-flow read-outs built from official pace and efficiency inputs, including probability of a close game, a blowout and overtime.
The full 51-game out-of-sample log, with the official final score next to both forecasts.

recommended_next_actions.why: Until this exists, nothing here can be called profitable - only better than a naive model. Everything else is optimisation of an unvalidated target.

recommended_next_actions.action: Backfill results for 2026-10-20 to 2026-11-05 and re-cut the split
recommended_next_actions.why: Every game from 2026-11-06 onward is already in the test window, so this is now the only way to grow the sample. It would let the ratings window move earlier and the test window roughly double again.

recommended_next_actions.action: Work on probability calibration rather than point accuracy
recommended_next_actions.why: The model is better on MAE and RMSE and worse on Brier and log loss. The gap between those two facts is where the leverage is.
Turns the availability impact from a floor into a real number and lets the prop strategies be graded.
The only way to grade the availability strategy or to run the robustness gate.

bottom_line: Everything asked for exists and is live: originated lines for every upcoming slate up to three days ahead, singles, parlays and same-game parlays, player-prop combos, a validation gate set, correlation values, a luck decomposition, injury and rotation tracking, game-flow analysis, a leaderboard with reward tiers, a suggestions page with decision paths, and a questions page split by what is known and what is not. The window grew from 28 games to 51 during this build and one conclusion flipped as a result - which is the clearest possible demonstration of why nothing here is being promoted yet.
